question.value: What is the nature and origin of faint, extended dust continuum emission (the 'Halo') in the outer regions of the protoplanetary disks Elias 2-24, IM Lup, and DM Tau?

evidence.quote: We aim to investigate the nature and origin of faint, extended dust emission in the outer regions of protoplanetary disks, which we define as the “Halo”, using multiwavelength (sub)millimeter continuum observations of three systems: Elias 2–24, IM Lup, and DM Tau.
Some of the observations taken directly from previously published works are: Elias 2-24 from (cite: andrews2018) (2016.1.00484.L) and (cite: carvalho2024) (2017.1.01330.S, 2018.1.01198.S)
Some of the observations taken directly from previously published works are: Elias 2-24 from (cite: andrews2018) (2016.1.00484.L) and (cite: carvalho2024) (2017.1.01330.S, 2018.1.01198.S)
Some of the observations taken directly from previously published works are: Elias 2-24 from (cite: andrews2018) (2016.1.00484.L) and (cite: carvalho2024) (2017.1.01330.S, 2018.1.01198.S)
and DM Tau from (cite: teague2025) (2021.1.01123.L).

The continuum was extracted by flagging channels within $\pm$ 25 km s$^{-1}$ around the targeted emission lines, and the data were subsequently averaged over 125 MHz channel widths, following the same procedure as (cite: andrews2018).

baselines.value: contains short and long baseline data

evidence.quote: All observations contained short baseline data to be sensitive to larger spatial scales.

When the short baseline observations showed a flux variation greater than 10% relative to the long-baseline data, they were self-calibrated independently before being combined with the long-baseline data.
In addition, we only included observations with angular resolutions < 0.3”, which ensured that the compact inner disk features could be spatially separated from the faint extended emission.
We used 18 archival dust continuum observations of three protoplanetary disks: Elias 2-24, IM Lup, and DM Tau.
The source coordinates were determined by querying the GAIA DR3 archive (cite: gaiacollab2018) via the `astroquery` package.
We recovered the gap-ring pair D58 and B78, respectively, that was previously identified in (cite: dsharp2) (distance = 139 pc; (cite: gaiadr3)).

Some of the observations taken directly from previously published works are: Elias 2-24 from (cite: andrews2018) (2016.1.00484.L) and (cite: carvalho2024) (2017.1.01330.S, 2018.1.01198.S); IM Lup from (cite: oberg2021) (2018.1.01055.L), (cite: andrews2018) (2016.1.00484.L), and (cite: careno2024) (2019.1.01357.S); and DM Tau from (cite: teague2025) (2021.1.01123.L).

what.value: Disk inclination and position angles for Elias 2-24 (29.0°, 45.7°), IM Lup (47.5°, 144.5°), and DM Tau (36.0°, 155.6°)

evidence.quote: Specifically, we adopted an inclination angle and position angle of 29.0°and 45.7°for Elias 2-24, 47.5°and 144.5°for IM Lup (cite: dsharp2), and 36.0°and 155.6°for DM Tau (cite: curone2025), respectively.

what.value: Stellar luminosities for Elias 2-24 (6.03 +/- 2.88 L_odot), IM Lup (2.57 +/- 1.23 L_odot), and DM Tau (0.36 +/- 0.18 L_odot)

evidence.quote: We assume a Gaussian distribution for $L_\ast$, centered at 6.03 $L_\odot$, 2.57 $L_\odot$, and 0.36 $L_\odot$ for Elias 2-24, IM Lup, and DM Tau, respectively, following (cite: andrews2018) and (cite: jun2021).

what.value: Gas surface density profiles, scale radius R_c, power-law index, and disk gas masses for Elias 2-24 (0.038 M_odot), IM Lup (0.106 M_odot), and DM Tau (0.057 M_odot)

evidence.quote: For Elias 2-24, we assume a total gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100 and adopt the scale radius $R_\mathrm{c}$ and power law index from (cite: pinte2023).
For IM Lup and DM Tau, we utilize the $\Sigma_\mathrm{g}$ derived from dynamical gas mass estimates by (cite: martire2024) (with vertical stratification) and (cite: longarini2025), respectively.

what.value: Stellar masses for Elias 2-24 (0.78 M_odot), IM Lup (1.19 M_odot), and DM Tau (0.47 M_odot)

evidence.quote: For Elias 2-24, IM Lup and DM Tau, we adopt $M_{\star}$ of 0.78$^{+0.34}_{-0.13}$, 1.19$^{+0.002}_{-0.002}$, and 0.47$^{+0.014}_{-0.015}$ M$_{\odot}$, respectively (cite: andrews2018; martire2024; longarini2025).

what.value: Disk age estimates for Elias 2-24 (0.08 - 0.5 Myr), IM Lup (0.9 - 1.3 Myr), and DM Tau (2.9 - 6 Myr)

evidence.quote: We obtain $t_\mathrm{drift} = 8 \times 10^{3}$ yr and $t_\mathrm{grow} = 3 \times 10^{4}$ yr, both 1-2 orders of magnitude shorter than the estimated disk age of 0.08 - 0.5 Myr (cite: andrews2018).

The corresponding timescales are $t_\mathrm{drift} = 6 \times 10^{4}$ yr and $t_\mathrm{grow} = 3 \times 10^{4}$ yr, both approximately 1-2 orders of magnitude shorter than the estimated disk age of 0.9 - 1.3 Myr (cite: avenhaus2018).

The inferred timescales are $t_\mathrm{drift} = 8 \times 10^{4}$ yr and $t_\mathrm{grow} = 10^{4}$ yr, are again 1-2 orders of magnitude shorter than the estimated disk age of 2.9 - 6 Myr (cite: garufi2024).

pipeline_or_manual.value: manual self-calibration in CASA v6.5.4; ALMA pipeline self-calibration in CASA v6.6.1 for DM Tau Band 6 and 9 before concatenation and manual self-calibration

evidence.quote: To improve the quality of the ALMA data, we applied self-calibration with the Common Astronomy Software Applications v6.5.4 (`CASA`; (cite: McMullin2007)).

Furthermore, the Band 6 and 9 projects of DM Tau were self-calibrated individually with the ALMA pipeline in CASA v6.6.1 due to their high S/N and then self-calibrated again by the method above after concatenation.

self_calibration.value: Phase self-calibration starting with solint='inf' decreasing down to solint='int' cleaning to 1 sigma at each step, followed by one round of amplitude self-calibration with solint='inf'

evidence.quote: Several rounds of phase self-calibration were performed, starting with a solution interval of infinite and progressively decreasing (to multiples of the integration time and finally to `solint=‘int’`) until no further improvement in S/N was achieved.
After each step, the image was cleaned down to 1$\sigma$, and the resulting model was saved to the model column to compute the next calibration table.
A final round of amplitude self-calibration with an infinite solution interval was also applied.
The final imaging was performed with the `tclean` task in CASA v6.6.5.

deconvolver.value: mtmfs (nterms = 2) when spectral windows separated by > 10 GHz; multiscale otherwise

evidence.quote: When the spectral windows were separated by more than 10 GHz in frequency, the `mtmfs` deconvolver (cite: Rau2011) with `nterms` = 2 was used, assuming that the frequency dependence of the emission can be represented by a second-order Taylor expansion.
For datasets where the spectral windows were closer in frequency, the `multiscale` deconvolver was adopted.
For each observation, several Briggs weighting values were tested to achieve an optimal balance between sensitivity and angular resolution.

analysis_steps.goal: Extract radial intensity, brightness temperature, and spectral index profiles, and measure disk sizes and halo fluxes

method.value: Deproject images using literature inclination and PA, azimuthally average in radial annuli, compute brightness temperature using the full Planck function, compute spectral index profiles, and integrate flux densities to determine R_68, R_90, R_99 and halo flux.

evidence.quote: After imaging, we generate azimuthally averaged intensity profiles by deprojecting the images using the disk’s inclination and position angle derived from literature.

The disk sizes $R_{68}$, $R_{90}$, and $R_{99}$, estimated as the radius enclosing 68%, 90%, and 99% of the total flux density, are computed for the most sensitive observation and are listed in Table 1.

From these profiles, we derive the brightness temperature profiles using the full Planck function, since we employ 0.45 mm data (ALMA Band 9) where the assumptions of low temperature and low frequency inherent to the Rayleigh–Jeans approximation no longer hold.

key_parameters.value: Halo starting radii: 86 au (Elias 2-24), 150 au (IM Lup), 130 au (DM Tau); outer boundary at 3 sigma_I of least sensitive observation (150, 300, 300 au)

evidence.quote: The outer boundary of the halo is defined as the radius at which the azimuthally averaged intensity profile of the least sensitive observation drops to 3$\sigma_\mathrm{I}$, where $\sigma_\mathrm{I}$ is the rms of the respective intensity profile.
extending outward to the largest radius where emission is detected in the least sensitive observation i.e. 150, 300, and 300 au for Elias 2-24, IM Lup, and DM Tau, respectively

evidence.quote: Specifically, we adopted an inclination angle and position angle of 29.0°and 45.7°for Elias 2-24, 47.5°and 144.5°for IM Lup (cite: dsharp2), and 36.0°and 155.6°for DM Tau (cite: curone2025), respectively.

analysis_steps.goal: Perform multiwavelength radial SED fitting to infer dust properties and select dust composition

method.value: Fit 1D vertically isothermal slab model with scattering independently at each radial step (from r = 11 au outward in steps of 1/3 smoothed beam) for four dust compositions using MCMC, apply double-resolution fitting for Elias 2-24 and DM Tau, compare models via Bayes factors, and integrate Sigma_d to obtain total and halo dust masses.

evidence.quote: In this work, we model the azimuthally averaged radial intensity profiles at each wavelength by assuming an axisymmetric, geometrically thin, and vertically isothermal disk.
In this work, we fit our free parameters using four dust compositions: DSHARP with no porosity, DSHARP with 70% porosity, ZUBKO with no porosity, and ZUBKO with 70% porosity.
Once we had the fits for all four dust compositions, we computed the Bayesian evidence of each MCMC fit with 500 random samples from the posterior.

key_parameters.value: 32 walkers, 5000 steps after 1000 burn-in steps, repeated a second time around median values; radial step = 1/3 smoothed resolution starting from r = 11 au

evidence.quote: We first run the fit with 32 walkers for 5000 steps, following a burn-in phase of 1000 steps.

To reduce the impact of low probability multi-modal solutions, we perform a second run initialized around the median values from the first run, extending for 5000 steps after an additional burn-in of 1000 steps.
The profiles are sampled in radial steps of $n$, where $n$ corresponds to one-third of the spatial resolution of the smoothed images.

assumptions.value: Power-law grain size distribution n(a) propto a^-q; Bruggeman and Maxwell-Garnett mixing rules for opacities; bulk densities 1.675, 0.503, 2.036, 0.611 g cm^-3 for the four compositions

evidence.quote: For a given composition and assuming a power–law grain size distribution $n(a) \propto a^{-q}$, where $a$ is the particle radius, the absorption and scattering opacities are calculated as functions of the maximum grain size $a_\mathrm{max}$ and the power law slope $q$.
For DSHARP (compact), DSHARP (70% porosity), ZUBKO (compact), and ZUBKO (70% porosity), $\rho_{{m}}$ is 1.675, 0.503, 2.036, and 0.611 g cm$^{-3}$, respectively.

assumptions.value: Constant Sigma_d extrapolated inward from 11 au to 0 au for total dust mass calculation

evidence.quote: To calculate the total dust mass of the disk, we extrapolated $\Sigma_\mathrm{d}$ inward from 11 au down to the disk center using the same radial spacing as the rest of the grid, assuming a constant surface density equal to the value at 11 au.

fitting.value: MCMC with emcee; Gaussian likelihood including absolute flux calibration uncertainty; radiative equilibrium temperature prior on T_d (3 to 100 K) with flaring angle 0.02-0.05 and Gaussian L_*; uniform priors on Sigma_d (10^-4 to 30 g cm^-2), log a_max (10^-3 to 10^2 cm), and q (1 to 4.5)

evidence.quote: We explored the parameter space using the Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method implemented through the `emcee` package (cite: emcee).

validation.value: Integrated autocorrelation times in the range 60 - 80 steps; Bayes factor comparison using 500 posterior samples relative to DSHARP (compact)

evidence.quote: Across all radii and disks, the integrated autocorrelation times typically lie in the range of 60 - 80 steps, indicating that the number of steps satisfies standard convergence criteria.
Once we had the fits for all four dust compositions, we computed the Bayesian evidence of each MCMC fit with 500 random samples from the posterior.

analysis_steps.goal: Compute gas-to-dust ratios, Stokes numbers, and dust drift and growth timescales

method.value: Combine inferred Sigma_d, T_d, and a_max with literature Sigma_g and stellar masses to compute gas-to-dust ratio (g2d), Stokes number (St), and drift and growth timescales (t_drift, t_grow), propagating uncertainties via 5000 bootstrap samples at each radius.

evidence.quote: Following the SED modeling, we calculate $g2d$ (the gas-to-dust ratio) given by $\Sigma_\mathrm{g}/\Sigma_\mathrm{d}$, where $\Sigma_\mathrm{g}$ is the gas surface density.

To propagate uncertainties into the timescales, we perform bootstrapping with 5000 samples at each radius, drawing $\Sigma_\mathrm{d}$, $\Sigma_\mathrm{g}$, $T_\mathrm{d}$, St, and $M_{\star}$ from gaussian distributions defined by their lower and upper bounds.

key_parameters.value: 5000 bootstrap samples per radius; turbulent viscosity alpha_t sampled uniformly in 10^-4 <= alpha_t <= 10^-2

evidence.quote: To propagate uncertainties into the timescales, we perform bootstrapping with 5000 samples at each radius, drawing $\Sigma_\mathrm{d}$, $\Sigma_\mathrm{g}$, $T_\mathrm{d}$, St, and $M_{\star}$ from gaussian distributions defined by their lower and upper bounds.
Due to the wide range of these estimates, we adopt a conservative range of $10^{-4} \le \alpha_\mathrm{t} \le 10^{-2}$ that we sample uniformly.

assumptions.value: Hydrostatic equilibrium and isothermal vertical structure for gas pressure; total g2d = 100 assumed for Elias 2-24; dynamical gas masses for IM Lup and DM Tau

findings_qualitative.value: The preferred dust compositions based on Bayes factors are ZUBKO (70% porosity) for Elias 2-24, ZUBKO (compact) for IM Lup, and DSHARP (compact) for DM Tau.

evidence.quote: By evaluating the Bayes factors relative to DSHARP (compact), we identify the preferred compositions for Elias 2-24, IM Lup, and DM Tau as ZUBKO (70% porosity), ZUBKO (compact), and DSHARP (compact), respectively.

findings_qualitative.value: A new gap and ring pair (D119 and B140) is identified in DM Tau at 0.45 mm (Band 9).

evidence.quote: Interestingly, despite the moderate resolution of our 0.45 mm data, we identify an additional gap and ring D119 and B140, respectively (distance = 144 pc; (cite: gaiadr3)).

findings_qualitative.value: The 0.45 - 0.9 mm spectral index profile in DM Tau exhibits values < 2 that can only be explained when dust scattering is included.

evidence.quote: In contrast, the halo of DM Tau exhibits $1 < \alpha < 2$ at 0.45 – 0.9 mm and $2 < \alpha < 4$ at 0.9 – 1.3 mm, a behavior that can only be explained when scattering is taken into account (cite: sierra2020).

claims.hypothesis: Extended outer dust halos hold a significant fraction of the total solid mass reservoir in protoplanetary disks and help alleviate the mass-budget problem.
claims.experiment: Measured halo flux densities across multiple ALMA bands and integrated radial dust surface density profiles derived from multiwavelength MCMC SED fitting.
claims.result: Halos account for 20-30% of the total continuum flux density and contain 33 (+12/-6), 103 (+25/-17), and 316 (+202/-117) M_oplus of dust in Elias 2-24, IM Lup, and DM Tau, corresponding to 26%, 34%, and 38% (25-40%) of the total disk dust mass.
claims.finding: Halos represent a substantial reservoir of solids (25-40% of total dust mass) that is often missed in shallower surveys and plays an important role in alleviating the mass-budget problem.

evidence.quote: The halos identified in our sources account for 20 - 30% of the total flux density at (sub)millimeter wavelengths.

As a result, halos make up 25 - 40% of the total dust content, demonstrating that they represent a substantial reservoir of solids and might play an important role in alleviating the mass-budget problem.

claims.hypothesis: Smooth outer dust halos in IM Lup and DM Tau are not in steady-state primordial viscous spreading, but instead originate from recent replenishment via late infall.
claims.experiment: Calculated local dust drift and growth timescales from SED-derived dust properties and dynamical gas surface densities, and compared them against stellar ages.
claims.result: In IM Lup and DM Tau, dust drift and growth timescales (~10^4 - 8x10^4 yr) are 1-2 orders of magnitude shorter than the disk ages, with t_grow <= t_drift, small maximum grain sizes (< 4 mm and < 9 mm), and low gas-to-dust ratios (64 and 18).
claims.finding: Because smooth primordial outer disks should rapidly grow and drift inward over timescales much shorter than the system ages, the persistence of small-grain halos in IM Lup and DM Tau favors relatively recent dust delivery via late infall.

evidence.quote: Our key result is that dust growth and drift timescales in the halos are 1–2 orders of magnitude shorter than the respective disk ages, indicating that the smooth outer disks should not exist.
The survival of their halos therefore favors a scenario in which the outer disks are replenished by relatively recent material delivery through late infall.

claims.hypothesis: The persistence of centimeter-sized grains in the halo of Elias 2-24 requires unresolved pressure traps in addition to possible late infall.
claims.experiment: Performed double-resolution multiwavelength SED fitting and timescale calculations for the halo of Elias 2-24.
claims.result: The halo of Elias 2-24 contains grains with a_max ~ 2 cm and exhibits t_drift = 8x10^3 yr and t_grow = 3x10^4 yr, which are 1-2 orders of magnitude shorter than its age of 0.08 - 0.5 Myr.
claims.finding: The presence of cm-sized grains combined with drift timescales much shorter than the disk age indicates that unresolved dust traps (potentially masked by high optical depth) must be slowing radial drift in Elias 2-24's halo.

evidence.quote: While the persistence of halos in IM Lup and DM Tau could be explained by late infall, the presence of centimeter-sized grains in Elias 2-24’s halo suggests that unresolved dust traps also play a role.

evidence.loc: Origin of halos - Evidence of late infall
evidence.quote: Such a short drift timescale relative to the system age, together with the cm-sized grains, indicates that hidden substructures, perhaps unresolved and affected by a high optical depth, must be slowing radial drift and keeping these grains in the halo.

why_this_data.value: Selected disks with smoothly declining outer continuum profiles beyond their outermost rings, archival coverage in at least three ALMA bands separated by > 20 GHz, angular resolution < 0.3" to separate inner features from the faint halo, and short-baseline data for large spatial scales.

evidence.quote: For the dust characterization, it was essential that each source had archival data in at least three ALMA bands.
In addition, we only included observations with angular resolutions < 0.3”, which ensured that the compact inner disk features could be spatially separated from the faint extended emission.
All observations contained short baseline data to be sensitive to larger spatial scales.

why_this_method.value: Used a 1D vertically isothermal slab model including anisotropic scattering because continuum emission traces the settled midplane and shorter wavelengths (e.g. 0.45 mm) require full Planck function and scattering; favored Bayes factor over chi^2 to naturally incorporate prior influence.

evidence.quote: From these profiles, we derive the brightness temperature profiles using the full Planck function, since we employ 0.45 mm data (ALMA Band 9) where the assumptions of low temperature and low frequency inherent to the Rayleigh–Jeans approximation no longer hold.
These assumptions are well justified at (sub)millimeter wavelengths, where the continuum emission primarily traces the midplane layer in which the largest dust grains have settled (cite: pinte2016).
We favor the Bayes factor over a traditional $\chi^{2}$ comparison because it naturally incorporates the influence of the prior.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Envelope contamination was ruled out based on axisymmetry, vertically thin geometry, and Keplerian rotation of the 12CO gas disk.

evidence.quote: We ruled out contamination of the extended emission by envelope emission based on its axisymmetry, vertically thin geometry, and Keplerian rotation of the $^{12}$CO gas disk well beyond the continuum emission (Elias 2-24: (cite: pinte2023); IM Lup: (cite: martire2024); DM Tau: (cite: longarini2025)).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Four dust compositions (DSHARP compact, DSHARP 70% porosity, ZUBKO compact, ZUBKO 70% porosity) were tested and three rejected per target based on Bayes factors and physical consistency.

evidence.quote: In this work, we fit our free parameters using four dust compositions: DSHARP with no porosity, DSHARP with 70% porosity, ZUBKO with no porosity, and ZUBKO with 70% porosity.

By evaluating the Bayes factors relative to DSHARP (compact), we identify the preferred compositions for Elias 2-24, IM Lup, and DM Tau as ZUBKO (70% porosity), ZUBKO (compact), and DSHARP (compact), respectively.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Stopped self-calibration rounds when S/N no longer improved; verified MCMC convergence via integrated autocorrelation times of 60-80 steps over 5000 steps.

evidence.quote: Several rounds of phase self-calibration were performed, starting with a solution interval of infinite and progressively decreasing (to multiples of the integration time and finally to `solint=‘int’`) until no further improvement in S/N was achieved.
Across all radii and disks, the integrated autocorrelation times typically lie in the range of 60 - 80 steps, indicating that the number of steps satisfies standard convergence criteria.

limitations_admitted.value: Substructures in smooth outer disks may remain undetected due to limited spatial resolution or high optical depth, making halo definition ambiguous.

evidence.quote: Recent studies suggest that substructures in smooth disks may remain undetected due to limited resolution (cite: alvarado2025; quincy2026) or high optical depth (e.g., MP Mus; (cite: ribas2025)), in which case defining a halo would be ambiguous.

limitations_admitted.value: Smoothing images to a common beam introduces beam dilution, which suppresses brightness temperatures and affects inner disk modeling when each radius is fitted independently without beam convolution.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, smoothing the images introduces beam dilution, which can suppress the brightness temperature. This effect is an inherent limitation of our modeling approach.
The model is not convolved with the beam, since each radius is fitted independently.

limitations_admitted.value: The 0.45 mm (Band 9) observation of DM Tau may trace a different vertical layer of the disk than longer wavelengths due to higher optical depth.

evidence.quote: These substructures are not evident in the 0.9 mm and 1.3 mm profiles, despite their higher resolution, indicating that the 0.45 mm observations might trace a different vertical layer of the disk due to its higher optical depth (see Fig. [\[fig:optical_depth\]](#fig:optical_depth) in Appendix [\[appendix_opacity\]](#appendix_opacity) where $\tau \sim 0.3$ near B140).

limitations_admitted.value: In the halos of IM Lup and DM Tau, a_max and q are largely unconstrained (uncertainties of ~1 dex in a_max and ~1.2 in q), which propagates into large uncertainties in Stokes numbers.

evidence.quote: At r < 90 au, $a_\mathrm{max}$ is $\sim$ 10 cm with an uncertainty of 0.7 dex, whereas at larger radii $a_\mathrm{max}$ remains mostly unconstrained with median values at 400 $\mu$m and uncertainties of 1 dex.

Due to the larger uncertainties in $a_\mathrm{max}$, the inferred St carries significant uncertainties; however, throughout most of the halo we find St $\leq 1$, consistent with marginal dust–gas coupling.

referee_caveats_inferred: For Elias 2-24, the gas surface density is not measured dynamically in the same way as IM Lup and DM Tau, but instead assumes a global gas-to-dust ratio of 100, making its halo gas-to-dust ratio (~196) dependent on that prior assumption.
Total dust masses rely on extrapolating a constant dust surface density from r = 11 au inward to r = 0 au, though the inner disk contribution to total area is small.
Ad-hoc modifications were required in the SED fitting for Elias 2-24 (penalizing T_d outside 5th-95th percentiles) and DM Tau (restricting Sigma_d upper bound around B24 to 10 g cm^-2).
